title: Vortex identification (Q and lambda2 iso-surfaces): where are the coherent structures?
summary: A three-dimensional view of the region where a vortex criterion exceeds a threshold, so the tube-like structures of a turbulent flow stand out from the background. The threshold decides what you see.

media.alt: Three-dimensional point cloud of elongated vortex tubes where the Q criterion exceeds a threshold, coloured by Q, with an annotation of the threshold.
media.caption: Reference render with synthetic demonstration data (design-system gallery).

source.note: Plot class from the design system's plot taxonomy; synthetic demonstration data.

read_the_figure.question: Where are the coherent structures?
read_the_figure.axes: x/D, y/D, z/D: the three coordinates in diameters. Colour: Q in 1/s^2 shown only where Q exceeds the threshold (here 0.5 Q_max). Marks: points sampled on the iso-region.
look_at: Are the structures elongated tubes, and in which direction do they run?
What is the threshold, and is it stated on the figure?
Is Q positive everywhere shown? Q > 0 means rotation beats strain.
Does the colour (strength) vary along a tube or between tubes?
read_the_figure.proves: It shows where rotation dominates strain, so where vortices are, and how they are arranged. It does not show how strong the circulation is, and a different threshold gives a different picture.
if_wrong: Threshold missing: the picture cannot be reproduced.
A threshold so low that the structures merge into a blob, or so high that only fragments remain.
A single static viewpoint: tubes in front hide those behind.

terms.meaning: The 3 by 3 matrix of derivatives du_i/dx_j. Splits into a symmetric strain part S and an antisymmetric rotation part Omega.
Q = (|Omega|^2 - |S|^2) / 2. Positive Q marks regions where rotation exceeds strain.
The second eigenvalue of S^2 + Omega^2; negative lambda2 marks a vortex core.
Surface on which a field equals one value (the threshold). The vortex is drawn inside it.
A flow region with a persistent organised motion, such as a vortex tube or a hairpin.

remember: Q > 0: rotation wins. Q = 0: pure shear. Solid-body rotation of rate Omega gives Q = Omega^2.
Rotate the view or use slices: depth is ambiguous.

understand.title: Marks and encodings
understand.text: Position gives the three coordinates; the cloud of points marks where Q exceeds the threshold, and colour (dark to yellow) encodes the local value of Q. The amber text at the top is the threshold annotation. The cube grid gives the frame. There is no surface shading here, so the structures read as point clouds.

understand.title: Why this form answers the question
understand.text: The velocity gradient tensor is nine numbers at each point of a 3D field and contains vortices and shear together. Q reduces it to one scalar that is positive where rotation dominates, and a threshold turns that scalar into a shape: the eye can follow tubes and count them. The idea is purely kinematic, which is why it is so widely used.

understand.title: Read this reference render
understand.text: Q1: What is the threshold? The amber label says Q = 0.5 Q_max, so only the strongest half of the Q range is drawn. Q2: What do the structures look like? Roughly seven elongated groups running along x (from x/D of 0 to about 3.5), wiggling in y and z, as streamwise tubes would. Q3: What does the colour tell you? The colour bar runs from about 0.7 to 1.95 1/s^2: yellow cores are the strongest rotation, blue-purple ends the weakest. A reader should also notice that 0.5 times the top of the bar is about 0.98, higher than the bottom of the bar, so the stated threshold and the plotted data do not agree.

understand.title: The must-check list, explained
understand.text: Threshold stated: the sentence in amber is what makes the figure reproducible. A vortex picture without a threshold can be made to show almost anything.

understand.title: How it misleads
understand.text: A threshold is a choice. A low value merges neighbouring structures and a high value cuts tubes into pieces, and 0.5 Q_max in this figure is a choice, not a law. Q is not Galilean invariant under rotation of the frame, and it is blind to strength of circulation. A 3D point cloud hides depth: structures in front mask those behind. Colour by Q suggests physical strength where there is only a criterion. In this render the colour bar minimum (about 0.65) is below 0.5 times the colour bar maximum (about 1.95, which would be about 0.98): the label and the data do not match, an example of why the threshold must be checked.

understand.title: Alternatives
understand.text: Surface rendering of the iso-surface with lighting; slices of Q at several planes; vorticity magnitude iso-surfaces (which show shear layers as well as vortices); the lambda2 or Delta criteria.

understand.title: A variant to create
understand.text: Draw the same field at three thresholds (0.2, 0.5, 0.8 Q_max) side by side, with a fixed camera.

steps.title: Decomposition of the velocity gradient
steps.tex: \nabla\mathbf u=\mathbf S+\boldsymbol\Omega,\quad S_{ij}=\tfrac12\Big(\tfrac{\partial u_i}{\partial x_j}+\tfrac{\partial u_j}{\partial x_i}\Big),\quad \Omega_{ij}=\tfrac12\Big(\tfrac{\partial u_i}{\partial x_j}-\tfrac{\partial u_j}{\partial x_i}\Big)
steps.note: Symmetric part is strain, antisymmetric part is rotation.

worked.title: Q for solid-body rotation and for simple shear
worked.problem: Compute Q for u = (-Omega y, Omega x) with Omega = 2 1/s, and for u = (gamma y, 0) with gamma = 3 1/s.

solution.text: Rotation: the gradient is antisymmetric, so S = 0 and the squared norm of the rotation tensor is 2 Omega^2.
Shear: S and Omega have equal norm, each equal to gamma^2 over 2.

worked.answer: Q = 4 1/s^2 for the rotating flow and 0 for pure shear: Q > 0 marks vortices only, and not every shear layer.

analyze.q: If you halve the threshold, what happens to the tubes?
A shear layer has large vorticity but Q = 0. Why does that matter for vortex identification?

Colour the structures by streamwise vorticity instead of Q: what new information appears?

checks.answer: Rotation rate squared exceeds strain rate squared: vortex-like motion.

checks.q: A published figure shows iso-surfaces with no stated threshold. How would you judge it?
checks.answer: Treat it as a sketch: the structures can be made fatter or thinner by the threshold, so ask for it and for a second threshold before comparing it with anything.
